cohort: The study cohort consisted of 1365 pregnant women diagnosed with vitamin D deficiency at 12-14 weeks of gestation in a single tertiary hospital in Chengdu, China, with 537 propensity-score matched pairs analyzed.
finding: Daily supplementation of 800IU of vitamin D improved depressive symptoms in pregnant women who were vitamin D deficient in early pregnancy and achieved vitamin D insufficiency after supplementation during the prenatal period.
gest_age: Participants were initially diagnosed at 12-14 weeks gestation, started supplementation from 14 weeks onwards, and were re-measured at a median gestational week 39 prior to delivery.
